pages.lead: You draw one box on frame 1 — no detector, no labels, no class. A discriminative correlation filter (KCF, CSRT) learns that patch and re-finds it every frame, at hundreds of frames per second. Here's the trick that makes it work, and why it's faster than it has any right to be.

pages.h1: Where it fails, changing backgrounds, and the drone problem
pages.lead: The same things that make correlation filters fast make them brittle. A taxonomy of how they lose the target, a straight answer on whether they survive a changing background, a worked verdict on tracking a maneuvering drone, and the trackers that fixed each weakness.
